A1.justification: Both complete 15-page PDFs describe the same Template Infilling study. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover the main paper, references, Appendices A–C, equations, figures, tables, and Algorithm 1. The only visible difference is the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of Template Infilling with LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B, including benchmark scores, ablations, robustness analyses, and qualitative examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, robustness analyses, and qualitative examples reported in v2, including the appendix results.

M1.justification: Template Infilling and Dynamic Segment Allocation are identical in Section 3 and Appendix C, including anchor placement, confidence-triggered mask expansion, and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both evaluate GSM8K, MATH500, HumanEval, and Trip Planning, and retain the same toxic-substance and phishing safety scenarios and appendix examples.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Vanilla and Prefix Prompting remain the benchmark baselines, with the same comparison configurations in the ablations and qualitative examples.

E3.justification: Both retain the same model variants, 128-token parallel-generation setup, evaluation metrics, and generation-length and sampling-step experiments. No stated evaluation settings change.

E4.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same component ablations and anchor-position sensitivity tests. Figures 3–5 and Appendices A–B preserve the same robustness studies, generation-order analysis, and qualitative cases.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results, and qualitative responses match. For example, Table 1 retains Dream-7B Base GSM8K scores of 8.87 for Vanilla, 8.79 for Prefix Prompting, and 44.58 for TI.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains identical mathematical definitions, Equations 1–5, generation-pathway reasoning, and confidence-based expansion assumptions. No proofs or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about structural conditioning, a 9.40-percentage-point average gain, accelerated sampling stability, and System-2 reasoning.

C2.justification: The sampling-prior and safety interpretations are unchanged, as are the instruction-tuning limitation in Section 6 and the autonomous-template-generation discussion in Section 5.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including static task templates, expansion of up to eight tokens per step with ten expansions, the official-codebase statement, and Appendix C pseudocode.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are identical, including comparisons with block diffusion, planning, constrained decoding, and conventional text infilling.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv v2 dated 7 April 2026 to v3 dated 18 May 2026. This is an administrative text update; all prose, headings, terminology, and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5, Tables 1–5, and Algorithm 1 retain identical rendering, captions, and placement. Pagination and the main-text and appendix layouts also match.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, supporting evidence, exposition, and figures and tables are identical, including Appendices A–C. Updating only the arXiv version/date stamp does not meaningfully improve or diminish the paper's overall quality.
